- **Orchard St Homecare caregiver-simulator audit and refactor plan:** Completed on 2026-10-09 in `~/.zeta/scratch/orchard_simulator_audit.md` after the predecessor worker stopped on a network error. The read-only audit found inactive scheduling, poor acceptance, hardcoded and lexical behavior, weak readiness and failure visibility, transport-boundary risks, compatibility debt, and test/evaluation gaps. As observed on 2026-10-09, the latest daily run was 37 days old; 26 of 202 linked callout responses (12.9%) were `available_interested`, 162 (80.2%) were `pending` or `no_response`, and the last 54 live daily runs averaged 10.4 important failures. The last-90-day history included 559 important failures, including 180 callout outcome timeouts and 161 shift-confirmation outcome timeouts. Production `auto_send_all_replies` was false despite a seed default of true. The proposed refactor separates cooperative demo behavior from adverse stress behavior, introduces one typed behavior profile and structural dispositions before language generation, improves run health and ledgers, reduces model and telephony cost, and splits orchestration into smaller modules. Estimated measured-component savings are approximately $9.1–$11.1/month (64–78%), excluding most caregiver-model spend. The audit also found regex-based voice opt-out inference controlling call behavior, persona behavior and scenario facts hardcoded in source prompts, and canned world-event content. Open decisions include exact response and positive-outcome targets, whether stress behavior uses a separate organization, retention of employee self-demo records, full-run cadence, voice-smoke cadence, configuration ownership, telemetry retention, and Luna approval after a provider-backed behavior gate. No repository files changed; no tests, calls, SMS, outreach, or simulations were performed, and production access was read-only.

- **Jev Terra-versus-Claude disagreement analysis:** Completed in PR #19678 at head `08428cff98`, squash-merged with merge commit `50c58187f9`. The protected analysis found that disagreements were primarily a policy-contract split rather than simple strictness: 81 of 128 primary disagreements involved hard-requirement scope or status, 14 involved ambiguous evidence, and the largest confusion cell contained 79 Terra `insufficient_evidence` versus Claude `poor` pairs. The proposed contract fixes define explicit hard-requirement decision order, the hard-requirement/preference boundary, and material-conflict and positive-support thresholds. The estimated upper-bound agreement after policy fixes is 52.5%, up from 36.0%, but this is a category-level counterfactual pending rerun after spot-check and contract revision. Protected artifacts used mode `0700` for the directory and mode `0600` for files; 12 assertions and formatting checks passed, with no additional paid spend. No repository or provider-backed tests were run because the change is a Markdown analysis note. A follow-up fit-contract-v2 worker is active on branch `agent/jev-fit-contract-v2`, with a $6 spend cap for rerunning Terra and Claude on the same 200 pairs.
